+## The run seed (#1949)
+
+Every randomized input in every test derives from one seed per run,
+carried by the `MCPX_TEST_SEED` env var — the only channel. The
+derivation (root, per-test streams, shuffle) is #1949 section 2,
+implemented in `internal/testsupport/gen` (streams) and
+`internal/testsupport/seed` (this transport: the lazy helper a test
+calls as `seed.Source(t, "name", version)`; it reads the env var
+only when a test actually asks, so unrelated packages stay
+cacheable, and on failure it logs the exact replay command).
+
+- **Locally**, run tests through the wrapper:
+  `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh [go test args...]`. It mints one
+  UUIDv7 seed if unset, exports it to every test process, derives
+  `-shuffle` from the same seed, prints the seed, and records it in
+  the gitignored `.cache/test-seed/` (`last` + `history`). Replay a
+  failure with one command:
+  `MCPX_TEST_SEED=<id> pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh -run '^TestX$' ./internal/<pkg>`.
+- **Bare `go test`** still works, with a limitation: with no seed
+  set, the helper mints one *per package process* and warns — a
+  bare run is reproducible from the printed id, but it is not one
+  seed per run. Use the wrapper when the run is the unit of
+  reproduction.
+- **In CI** the workflows mint once per run (the `seed` job in
+  `mcpx.yml`, the `init` job in `mcpx-test.yml`) and pass the id to
+  every `go test` job; a `workflow_dispatch` `seed` input replays a
+  previous run exactly, and re-running failed jobs reuses the
+  original seed because the successful seed job is not re-run. CI
+  never mints inside a test process: unset in CI, the helper and
+  the wrapper both fail closed. `mcpx.yml` uploads the run's
+  `seed.json` as the `test-seed` artifact, which the seed collector
+  (#1953) files into `testdata/seeds/v1`.
+- The seed reproduces inputs and test order, not timing (#1949
+  section 6 caveat).
+
 ## Finding the tests that touch a change (Approach C, decided #1966)
 
 `scripts/affected-tests.py` (dry-run by default; `--run` executes):

+// Package seed is the lazy run-seed helper for mcpx's randomized
+// tests (#1949 section 4, Approach C): the one channel by which the
+// per-run seed reaches a test process is the MCPX_TEST_SEED env var,
+// and this package is its only reader.
+//
+// Why lazy: a package that never calls this helper never reads the
+// env var, so its test results stay cacheable by go test (a test
+// that reads an env var is cached keyed on that var's value; the
+// packages that do use randomness are exactly the ones that must
+// re-run when the seed changes). There is no TestMain anywhere.
+//
+// Behaviour by situation (#1949 section 5):
+//
+//   - MCPX_TEST_SEED set (wrapper locally, the seed job in CI):
+//     used as-is after validation. On input any string matching
+//     [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128} is accepted, so a human can replay an
+//     old id; only the wrapper and CI mint, and they mint UUIDv7.
+//   - Unset outside CI (bare go test): a seed is minted once per
+//     process and a warning is logged on first use — reproducible
+//     (the id is printed on failure), but per-package, which is
+//     why the wrapper (pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh) is the entrypoint
+//     that gives one seed per run.
+//   - Unset in CI (CI=true or GITHUB_ACTIONS=true): fail closed.
+//     CI must never mint inside a test process; the workflow's
+//     seed job mints once per run and passes the id down.
+//
+// Allowlist note (#172): MCPX_TEST_SEED is a test-only variable —
+// it is read only here, under internal/testsupport, and no setting
+// declares it (the MCPX_TEST_* prefix is reserved for this class;
+// no settings path may start with test.). This comment is the
+// allowlist entry the env-inventory guard points at, in the same
+// shape as MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE's in internal/testsupport/require.go.
+package seed
+
+import (
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"regexp"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/developing-today/code/pkgs/mcpx/internal/testsupport/gen"
+)
+
+// EnvVar is the one channel: the run seed env var name.
+const EnvVar = "MCPX_TEST_SEED"
+
+// validID is the input contract (#1949 section 1): minting produces
+// canonical UUIDv7, but any id of this shape replays.
+var validID = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`)
+
+// Valid reports whether id is an acceptable run-seed id on input.
+func Valid(id string) bool { return validID.MatchString(id) }
+
+// Mint returns a new canonical lowercase UUIDv7 (RFC 9562 section
+// 5.7): 48-bit unix-millisecond timestamp, version 7, variant 10xx,
+// and every remaining bit from crypto/rand — 74 random bits, more
+// than google/uuid's NewV7 (which spends rand_a on sub-millisecond
+// clock precision). No dependency; the wrapper's python3 one-liner
+// and the CI mint step produce the same format.
+func Mint() string {
+	var b [16]byte
+	ms := uint64(time.Now().UnixMilli())
+	b[0], b[1], b[2] = byte(ms>>40), byte(ms>>32), byte(ms>>24)
+	b[3], b[4], b[5] = byte(ms>>16), byte(ms>>8), byte(ms)
+	if _, err := rand.Read(b[6:]); err != nil {
+		// crypto/rand failing is unrecoverable for minting; a
+		// time-only id would silently collide across runs.
+		panic(fmt.Sprintf("seed: crypto/rand: %v", err))
+	}
+	b[6] = b[6]&0x0f | 0x70 // version 7
+	b[8] = b[8]&0x3f | 0x80 // variant 10xx
+	return fmt.Sprintf("%x-%x-%x-%x-%x", b[0:4], b[4:6], b[6:8], b[8:10], b[10:16])
+}
+
+// Shuffle derives the go test -shuffle value for a run seed
+// (#1949 section 2): int64(big-endian(SHA-256(root || "shuffle")[:8])
+// & MaxInt63), where root is gen.Root(seed). The wrapper script and
+// the CI stress jobs implement the same formula in python3; the
+// three implementations are pinned to each other by this package's
+// tests (which restate the formula from the spec, not from gen).
+func Shuffle(seed string) int64 {
+	root := gen.Root(seed)
+	h := sha256.Sum256(append(root[:], []byte("shuffle")...))
+	return int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(h[:8]) & (1<<63 - 1))
+}
+
+// resolveFrom is the resolution policy over an env getter, split
+// out so tests can drive every branch without the process-wide
+// once. minted reports whether the id was minted here (bare go
+// test), which is the case the caller must warn about.
+func resolveFrom(get func(string) string) (id string, minted bool, err error) {
+	if v := get(EnvVar); v != "" {
+		if !Valid(v) {
+			return "", false, fmt.Errorf("seed: %s=%q is not a valid seed id ([A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128})", EnvVar, v)
+		}
+		return v, false, nil
+	}
+	if get("CI") == "true" || get("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true" {
+		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("seed: %s is unset in CI; CI must never mint inside a test process — the workflow seed job (or the wrapper outside CI) provides it", EnvVar)
+	}
+	return Mint(), true, nil
+}
+
+var (
+	once     sync.Once
+	resolved string
+	resErr   error
+)
+
+// Run returns this process's run seed, resolving MCPX_TEST_SEED
+// lazily on first use (see the package comment for the policy). It
+// fails the test on any resolution error: in CI that is the
+// fail-closed rule, and an invalid id is never silently replaced.
+func Run(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	once.Do(func() {
+		var minted bool
+		resolved, minted, resErr = resolveFrom(os.Getenv)
+		if resErr == nil && minted {
+			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "seed: no %s; generated %s for this package only — use pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh for one seed per run\n", EnvVar, resolved)
+		}
+	})
+	if resErr != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("%v", resErr)
+	}
+	return resolved
+}
+
+// Source returns the gen.Source stream for (this test,
+// generator name@version) under the run seed — the lazy helper
+// #1949 section 4 specifies. It registers a cleanup that, if the
+// test failed, logs the seed, test and generator plus the exact
+// one-command replay (#1949 section 6).
+func Source(t *testing.T, name string, version int) gen.Source {
+	t.Helper()
+	id := Run(t)
+	src := gen.ForTest(t, id, name, version)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		if t.Failed() {
+			t.Logf("seed: reproduce with: %s=%s pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh -run '^%s$' <package> (seed %s, test %s, generator %s@%d)", EnvVar, id, t.Name(), id, t.Name(), name, version)
+		}
+	})
+	return src
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# lane-scratch: n/a — repo file (pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh), queue task 13250
+# test.sh — the mcpx test entrypoint (#1949, Approach C): one run
+# seed per run, for every go test process this wrapper starts.
+#
+#   pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh [go test args...]
+#
+# With no args it runs the whole suite (go test ./...). Any args are
+# passed to go test verbatim, after the derived -shuffle flag:
+#
+#   pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh -run '^TestX$' ./internal/codegen
+#
+# The seed (MCPX_TEST_SEED, #1949 section 4) is minted once here —
+# never inside a test process — exported to every go test process
+# (and, via os.Environ in the e2e harness, to every subprocess), and
+# printed so a failure replays with one command:
+#
+#   MCPX_TEST_SEED=<id> pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh -run '^TestX$' ./internal/codegen
+#
+# Behaviour (#1949 section 5):
+#   - MCPX_TEST_SEED set: validated ([A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}) and used
+#     as-is; an invalid value is an error, never a silent re-mint.
+#   - Unset locally: warn, mint a UUIDv7, print it, and record it in
+#     the gitignored pkgs/mcpx/.cache/test-seed/ (last + history).
+#   - Unset in CI (CI=true or GITHUB_ACTIONS=true): exit 1. CI mints
+#     in the workflow's seed job, once per run, and passes the id
+#     down — a test process must never mint its own.
+#
+# -shuffle is derived from the same seed (#1949 section 2), so the
+# seed alone reproduces both the generated inputs and the test
+# order. Caveat (#1949 section 6): this reproduces inputs and
+# order, not timing. Bare `go test` without the wrapper still works
+# — the seed helper then mints per package process and warns; the
+# wrapper is what makes the seed per-run instead of per-package.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+
+mint_v7() {
+  python3 -c "import os,time;b=bytearray(int(time.time()*1000).to_bytes(6,'big')+os.urandom(10));b[6]=b[6]&15|0x70;b[8]=b[8]&63|0x80;h=b.hex();print(f'{h[:8]}-{h[8:12]}-{h[12:16]}-{h[16:20]}-{h[20:]}')"
+}
+
+if [ -z "${MCPX_TEST_SEED:-}" ]; then
+  if [ "${CI:-}" = "true" ] || [ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" = "true" ]; then
+    echo "test.sh: MCPX_TEST_SEED is unset in CI; CI must never mint inside a test run — the workflow seed job provides it" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  MCPX_TEST_SEED="$(mint_v7)"
+  echo "test.sh: warning: no MCPX_TEST_SEED; minted $MCPX_TEST_SEED for this run" >&2
+  cache_dir=".cache/test-seed"
+  mkdir -p "$cache_dir"
+  printf '%s\n' "$MCPX_TEST_SEED" >"$cache_dir/last"
+  printf '%s\n' "$MCPX_TEST_SEED" >>"$cache_dir/history"
+fi
+
+if ! printf '%s' "$MCPX_TEST_SEED" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$'; then
+  echo "test.sh: MCPX_TEST_SEED=$MCPX_TEST_SEED is not a valid seed id ([A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128})" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+export MCPX_TEST_SEED
+
+# Shuffle derivation, #1949 section 2 — the same formula the Go
+# helper (internal/testsupport/seed.Shuffle) and the CI stress jobs
+# implement; the helper's tests pin the formula from the spec.
+shuffle="$(python3 -c "
+import hashlib, os
+root = hashlib.sha256(b'mcpx-test-seed/v1\x00' + os.environ['MCPX_TEST_SEED'].encode()).digest()
+print(int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(root + b'shuffle').digest()[:8], 'big') & (2**63 - 1))
+")"
+
+echo "MCPX_TEST_SEED=$MCPX_TEST_SEED (shuffle=$shuffle; reproduce: MCPX_TEST_SEED=$MCPX_TEST_SEED pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh <args>)"
+
+if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
+  set -- ./...
+fi
+exec go test -shuffle="$shuffle" "$@"

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Wrapper tests for pkgs/mcpx/scripts/test.sh (queue task 13250, issue #1949).
+
+The wrapper is the local half of the run-seed transport: it must
+mint or accept exactly one seed, export it to the go test process,
+derive -shuffle from that same seed by the #1949 section 2 formula,
+and fail closed in CI. Each test runs the real script with a fake
+`go` on PATH that records its argv and environment, so the oracle
+is what the test process would actually receive.
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s pkgs/mcpx/scripts/tests -p 'test_mcpx_test_seed.py' -v
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+import os
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+REPO_MCPX = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", ".."))
+SCRIPT = os.path.join(REPO_MCPX, "scripts", "test.sh")
+
+FAKE_GO = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf 'ARGS:%s\\n' "$*"
+printf 'SEED:%s\\n' "${MCPX_TEST_SEED:-<unset>}"
+"""
+
+
+def spec_shuffle(seed: str) -> int:
+    """The #1949 section 2 formula, restated from the issue text."""
+    root = hashlib.sha256(b"mcpx-test-seed/v1\x00" + seed.encode()).digest()
+    return int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(root + b"shuffle").digest()[:8], "big") & (2**63 - 1)
+
+
+class WrapperTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mcpx-test-seed-")
+        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp, True)
+        # The script cd's to pkgs/mcpx and writes .cache there when it
+        # mints; run it from a scratch copy so the tree stays clean.
+        self.work = os.path.join(self.tmp, "mcpx")
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.work, "scripts"))
+        shutil.copy2(SCRIPT, os.path.join(self.work, "scripts", "test.sh"))
+        bindir = os.path.join(self.tmp, "bin")
+        os.makedirs(bindir)
+        fake = os.path.join(bindir, "go")
+        with open(fake, "w") as fh:
+            fh.write(FAKE_GO)
+        os.chmod(fake, 0o755)
+        self.env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()
+                    if k not in ("MCPX_TEST_SEED", "CI", "GITHUB_ACTIONS")}
+        self.env["PATH"] = bindir + os.pathsep + self.env["PATH"]
+
+    def run_wrapper(self, args=(), **env):
+        e = dict(self.env, **env)
+        return subprocess.run(
+            ["bash", os.path.join(self.work, "scripts", "test.sh"), *args],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, env=e, timeout=60)
+
+    def test_set_seed_is_exported_and_derives_shuffle(self):
+        seed = "01a0f101-2378-7c1c-9dc1-5a1ae1571eca"
+        r = self.run_wrapper(["./internal/codegen"], MCPX_TEST_SEED=seed)
+        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
+        self.assertIn(f"SEED:{seed}", r.stdout)
+        self.assertIn(f"ARGS:test -shuffle={spec_shuffle(seed)} ./internal/codegen", r.stdout)
+
+    def test_unset_locally_mints_v7_and_records_it(self):
+        r = self.run_wrapper()
+        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
+        m = re.search(r"SEED:([0-9a-f-]{36})", r.stdout)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(m, r.stdout + r.stderr)
+        seed = m.group(1)
+        self.assertEqual(seed[14], "7", seed)          # version nibble
+        self.assertIn(seed[19], "89ab", seed)          # variant bits
+        self.assertIn(f"ARGS:test -shuffle={spec_shuffle(seed)} ./...", r.stdout)
+        with open(os.path.join(self.work, ".cache", "test-seed", "last")) as fh:
+            self.assertEqual(fh.read().strip(), seed)
+
+    def test_unset_in_ci_fails_closed(self):
+        for extra in ({"CI": "true"}, {"GITHUB_ACTIONS": "true"}):
+            r = self.run_wrapper(**extra)
+            self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1, extra)
+            self.assertIn("never mint", r.stderr)
+            self.assertNotIn("ARGS:", r.stdout)
+
+    def test_invalid_seed_is_an_error_not_a_remint(self):
+        r = self.run_wrapper(MCPX_TEST_SEED="bad seed!")
+        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1)
+        self.assertIn("not a valid seed id", r.stderr)
+        self.assertNotIn("ARGS:", r.stdout)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
